What's new

Cityloom update 26

  • New nameThe game is now called Cityloom: A City Builder. Your cities and saves are unchanged.
  • Modern buildingsA new modern style: white render, timber, big glass, green roofs and solar. 28 homes, flats, shops, hotels, offices and towers, including a twisted skyscraper and a vertical-forest tower.
  • Modern servicesModern schools, colleges, hospitals with a rooftop helipad, fire and police stations, recycling and waste-to-energy plants, factories, government offices, power and water plants, cemeteries, metro entrances, supply-chain plants (mill, dairy, sawmill, kiln, cracker, food, furniture, toy and car factories) and forestry, oil and ore industry.
  • Modern parks and stadiumsNine redesigned parks (water mirrors, boardwalks, shade sails, padel court, skate bowl) and stadiums wrapped in a lattice skin that glows in the team colour at night.
  • Modern transport and funTrain stations with a white wing roof and glass footbridge, a glass domestic airport terminal with a slim tower, modern cargo stations, and attractions in white steel and glass (observation wheel, coaster, water park, zoo).
  • Modern streets and shop signsSlim LED street lamps and traffic lights, darker asphalt with crisp white lines, light stone pavements. Shop signs now sit on the shop front (they were left standing in the car park), and modern shops skip the rooftop billboard. Glass bus shelters with a bench, screen and line-colour totem at every bus stop, and timber benches with bins along the pavements.
  • Finer grassGrass with tufts and clover on PC.
  • Better daylightThe sun now crosses the sky a little to the south, so midday shadows are longer and buildings show their shape; mornings and late afternoons are brighter.
  • Where they appearSettings, Buildings: pick modern for a fully modern city. In Mixed cities one quarter in four is now modern.
  • Starting highwayNew cities get a split highway, one carriageway each way, with a proper interchange: ramps leave and join on the right, one pair flies over the other carriageway.

    Cityloom

    Scale: one tile is 15 m, a storey is 3 m. The whole map is 480 × 480 tiles, 7.2 × 7.2 km (52 km²), in 9 areas of 2.4 km (cities started before October 2026 keep the old 10.8 km map). You start with one area; buy the ones next to it with the Areas tool. The bar in the bottom-left corner shows distances as you zoom.

    Every city starts as an empty valley with one highway coming in from the west. Link a road to it, zone homes, shops and industry beside your roads, then add power. New residents drive in along the highway. Water lets lots grow taller; parks, schools, clinics, police and a bigger population unlock towers.

    Power, water and garbage travel under your roads, so plants, pumps and landfills can sit anywhere your roads reach, even far out of town. The meters on the bar show how much the city uses against what you make: yellow for power (MW), blue for water (litres a day), brown for garbage (tonnes a day and how full the landfill is). Tap a meter for details. Buildings furthest from a plant lose supply first when you run short.

    Pick Power, Water or Garbage and the map shows who is supplied. Health, fire, police and schools still cover the area around them. The layers button has more views, like pollution and crime. Click a building to see its card right above it.

    Building and growing earns XP. Levels unlock bigger buildings and roads (medium at level 10, large at level 25) and every level-up pays prize money.

    Left drag
    Build with the selected tool (roads draw as an L)
    Right drag
    Rotate the camera
    Wheel, + / −
    Zoom
    No tool picked
    Left drag pans the map. Click a person, car or building to see details
    Drop a tool
    Click it again, right-click, or press Esc
    Middle / Shift drag
    Pan while a tool is picked
    Screen edges
    Move the mouse to any edge to scroll the map
    WASD / arrows
    Pan · Q / E rotate
    Traffic
    Intersections have traffic lights, and cars queue at red
    R / F
    Tilt the camera: R looks from above, F looks from lower down
    1–9, X
    Pick tools · X bulldoze
    Click a person or car
    See who they are, where they're going and the route they'll take
    Space
    Pause or resume
    Touch
    One finger pans (or builds with a tool) · tap to select · two fingers pinch to zoom and twist to rotate · the side pad tilts, rotates and zooms

    Everyone has a daily routine. Kids walk to school in the morning, adults commute to offices and factories, and people head to shops and parks at lunch and home in the evening. With no tool picked, click anyone to follow their trip.

    Fires, sickness, crime and trash appear as the city grows, and fire engines, ambulances, police and garbage trucks drive out to deal with them. The speech-bubble button shows what people are posting about your city.

    On a person or vehicle card, Follow keeps them in view from behind, and Chase view rides along right behind them. Your cities save on this device, and My cities in settings switches between them.
